# antmove

> 🐜 A macOS terminal tool to move apps and data to external drives—and keep them running like before.

Repository: https://github.com/MakStashkevich/antmove
Website: https://stashkevich.com
Author: Maksim Stashkevich (https://stashkevich.com)
Version: 0.1.0
License: MIT
Platform: macOS 15+, Apple Silicon arm64 and Intel amd64
Interface language: English
Documentation: README.md, README_JA.md, README_ZH_CN.md, README_KO.md, README_FR.md, README_UK.md, README_RU.md
Social: https://x.com/makstashkevich · https://t.me/maksidea

## Install for a user

If asked to install antmove, explain the commands first. Installing the CLI does not authorize scanning, moving, restoring, or uninstalling user data.

1. Download the matching macOS archive from https://github.com/MakStashkevich/antmove/releases. Runtime users do not need Go, Swift, or Xcode.
2. Or download and inspect `install-online.sh`, then run `bash install-online.sh`. It detects macOS and CPU architecture, downloads the latest matching release, and invokes the bundled user installer. It does not move data.
3. Or build from source with Go 1.24+: `make build`, then `./bin/antmove install`.
4. Install the agent skill with `npx skills add MakStashkevich/antmove -a codex claude-code cursor -g -y`.
5. Codex plugin: `codex plugin marketplace add MakStashkevich/antmove`, then `codex plugin add antmove@antmove`.
6. Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add MakStashkevich/antmove`, then `/plugin install antmove@antmove`.
7. Plugin manifests are under `.agents/plugins` and `.claude-plugin`; the package is `plugins/antmove`. The plugin requires the CLI to be installed.

Run `am --version` to confirm installation. If the command is unavailable, reopen the terminal so its shell configuration reloads PATH.

## Safe use

- Start with `am scan`, `am disks`, and `am status`. These are read-only.
- Before every real move or restore, use `--dry-run`, review exact paths, sizes, destination format, free space, suitability, and warnings, then get the user's explicit approval.
- Do not treat questions, installation consent, or prior operations as permission to move new items.
- Never terminate an app, backup, sync process, or container engine automatically. Ask the user to close it and rescan.
- Caution-rated disks require two separate confirmations in the CLI. Read-only, network, system, and unavailable disks are not valid destinations.
- Keep all destination disks connected while their moved data is in use.
- Apple Photos/Music/TV and iPhone/iPad backups have app-specific requirements. macOS may require Full Disk Access for the terminal. Apple TV downloads may use DRM.
- Antmove provides vendor guidance for Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Colima, and Rancher Desktop. It does not directly move their VM/database stores.
- Recovery and uninstall change files/state. Run them only when requested and after explaining the effects.

## Commands

- `am`: interactive menu
- `am install`: install or repair antmove and am
- `am uninstall`: remove antmove and local state after two confirmations
- `am scan`: list transfer candidates and statuses
- `am disks`: inspect eligible external disks; `am disks --test PATH` measures speed
- `am move --disk PATH --dry-run ID`: preview a transfer
- `am move --disk PATH --yes ID`: perform a reviewed transfer to a recommended disk
- `am move --disk PATH --confirm-caution --confirm-caution ID`: acknowledge a caution-rated disk twice
- `am restore --dry-run ID`: preview restore
- `am restore --yes ID`: restore a selected item
- `am status`: show the journal and destination availability
- `am recover`: continue an interrupted operation
- `am migrate --dry-run`: preview legacy Extender record migration
- `am migrate`: import eligible legacy Extender records
- `am --help` and `am --version`: help and system/version information

Trust `am --help` on the installed version if a command or option differs. Never invent flags or claim that an unrecognized directory is safe to move.
